title: Construction of the cocycle Leray edge
statement: For a morphism f:X to Y of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let H^q and R^q f_* be the module cohomology and higher direct image functors [pqf-def-cohomology] of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. There exists a family of natural homomorphisms from H^q(X,-) to global sections of R^q f_* satisfying the injective-resolution cocycle equation in the Lean signature: after identifying sections of the direct image [def-pc-module-pullback] with sections on X, each global cycle lifts to a section of the cycle sheaf and its edge value is its projected homology class, for every injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions].

proof.text: Choose an injective resolution $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ as in [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. By the definition of direct image, $\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet)=\Gamma(Y,f_*\mathcal I^\bullet)$ termwise. A cocycle in degree $q$ therefore represents a global section of $\ker(f_*\mathcal I^q\to f_*\mathcal I^{q+1})$, and its image in the quotient by the preceding image is the displayed cocycle formula for $\varepsilon^q_{\mathcal F}$. The identifications $H^q(X,\mathcal F)=H^q(\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet))$ and $R^qf_*\mathcal F=\mathcal H^q(f_*\mathcal I^\bullet)$ are the definitions of [pqf-def-cohomology] and higher direct image.

proof.text: Apply [thm-sp-grothendieck] to the composable pair $F=f_*:\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)\to\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y)$ and $G=\Gamma(Y,-):\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y)\to\mathrm{Ab}$. The hypotheses of [def-sp-composite-acyclicity] hold: $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ and $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y)$ are Grothendieck abelian by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] (the site of open subsets of a scheme is small and $\mathcal O_X$, $\mathcal O_Y$ are sheaves of commutative rings), $\mathrm{Ab}=\mathrm{Mod}(\mathbb Z)$ is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian], and $f_*$ and $\Gamma(Y,-)$ are additive and left exact because kernels in $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$, $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y)$ are computed sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The required acyclicity hypothesis is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pushforward-injective-acyclic] with $h=f$ and $V=Y$. Termwise $\Gamma(Y,f_*\mathcal G)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal G)$, so [pqf-def-cohomology] and [lem-sp-derived-well-defined] identify $R^n(G\circ F)(\mathcal F)$ with $H^n(X,\mathcal F)$ and $R^nF(\mathcal F)$ with $R^nf_*\mathcal F$. The left edge is functorial by [lem-sp-grothendieck-edge-maps], and its cocycle description is exactly [lem-pc-grothendieck-edge-cocycle]. Hence the displayed map is independent of the resolution and natural in $\mathcal F$.
